text:
Alex: Heads-up — starting at ~21:00 UTC we saw a sharp rise in GPU attach failures in us-west-2 and intermittent capacity alarms in eu-west-1. Errors are coming back as `GPU_RESERVE_EXHAUSTED` and connection timeouts.
Mira: I'm seeing the same in our dashboards — queue depth spiked after the canary scale-up. Latency for short sequences climbed. :grimacing:
Jordan: Any recent model pushes or config changes around capacity or weighted routing?
Alex: We rolled a canary with higher concurrency (model-variants: v3-hot) ~20:50 UTC. Traffic shift was 10% -> 35% for that variant. No infra deploys.
Samir: Ops telemetry shows reservation churn — warm pool drains faster than our refill TTL. Looks like we didn't account for bursty prefix reuse.
Kevin: Also noticed net egress saturation on the west aggregation layer around the same window. Might be compounding attach retries.
ops-bot: Alert: GPU reservation failures > 5% in us-west-2 for the last 3m. Auto-fallback engaged to compatible-cpu-fallback policy.
Mira: Immediate mitigation: can we pause canary expansion and reduce concurrency on v3-hot?
Alex: Paused the rollout and set concurrency cap to 4 for canary. Beginning manual redistribution of reserved capacity from non-critical pools.
Jordan: Can we run a quick script to bump anticipatory reserves for predicted 5m bursts? I have a small helper:
```
# quick reserve bump
./reservectl set anticipatory --region us-west-2 --slots 120 --ttl 300
```
Samir: Script ran, bump applied to us-west-2 for 2 minutes. Watching attachment success rate.
Kevin: After bump attach failures dropped to ~1.2% and queue depth started to fall. Network egress also normalized after temporary traffic shaping.
Alex: Good. Post-incident notes we should capture: 1) anticipatory reserve TTL too short, 2) warm pool refill thresholds not tuned for canary burst patterns, 3) routing weight change lacked a pre-check for reservation headroom.
Mira: Agreed. Proposed runbook changes: add a pre-shift check that computes projected reserve delta given planned weight changes, and require a green check from `reserve-sanity` before traffic shifts >10%.
Jordan: Also add a cost-aware knob: if anticipatory reserve would exceed X% of committed capacity, fail the pre-check and surface a blocking approval to SRE/Infra.
Samir: I'll open the playbook PR with: - pre-shift reserve calculation - mandatory concurrency caps for canaries - automatic temporary reserve bump script with safety TTL - network egress sanity step
Alex: Add an action item to increase default anticipatory TTL from 60s to 300s for regions with observed prefix reuse > 2.0.
Kevin: We should also log reserve decisions in the tracing headers so we can correlate client retries with reserve events.
Mira: For follow-ups: - Jordan to implement pre-shift check (owner: Jordan) - Samir to PR runbook edits (owner: Samir) - Alex to update alert thresholds and dashboard tiles (owner: Alex) - Kevin to add trace header logging (owner: Kevin)
ops-bot: Incident NOTABLE: failover fallback kicked in; no customer-facing SLA breach detected.
oncall-bot: Post-incident: please file a postmortem within 72h and add the rollout details to the RCA template.
Alex: Thanks all. I'll collate logs, attach the reservectl history, and file the postmortem. Closing thread after PRs and dashboards update. :white_check_mark:
